after_landing.notes: Archives the plan folder only when its gaps list has no open entry; with an open gap, skip this step and leave the folder live.

release_levels.reason: The parse check of each JSON, YAML and TOML target is new behavior: a render that does not parse now stops with code 2 and the old file stays.

units.title: The shared libraries common, write and select
Tests for the parse check and the header detection
units.waits: Its cases run the libraries that U1 creates and the repo-sync front-end that U1 changes.

shared_files.why: every human-facing doc; the earlier units report DOCS FALSIFIED lines and never edit a doc

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 moves code of the sync into three new libraries that each consumer runs, and U2 changes the test task. The plan lands runnable code, so one review unit in wave 3 covers U1 and U2.
decisions.rejected: No review unit (the wave review alone does not run /security-review).

decisions.decision: Do the 16 plans of the macos-setup merge run in parallel?
decisions.ruling: No. The 16 plans form one linear chain through requires, because most of them edit sync-engine/repo-sync or sync-engine/setup-sync, and parallel plans conflict there. This plan requires plan 1 only.

decisions.decision: Where do the tests of this plan go?
decisions.ruling: This plan extends test:repo-sync with cases for its new rules. A current case changes only where a ruling changes its expected result.

decisions.decision: Does the run sync bootstrap and its consumers?
decisions.ruling: No. mise run setup:configs in bootstrap and in each consumer stays a hand step (Out of scope), as in earlier plans.
decisions.rejected: A sync in an after-landing step.

decisions.decision: How does the shared log function get the name of its front-end?
decisions.ruling: _se_log prints '<prefix>: <text>' on stderr, with the prefix in the variable _SE_PREFIX. sync-engine/repo-sync sets _SE_PREFIX=repo-sync before its first call, so each message stays byte for byte as today.
decisions.rejected: A prefix argument on each call (every call site changes and the risk of a typo grows).

decisions.decision: Which format does a .json target with comments get?
decisions.ruling: A target with the extension .json gets the format json, except when the rendered file has a line that starts with // after spaces: that file is JSONC (the bootstrap header of a JSON file is a comment inside {), so its format is text. .vscode/settings.json and .vscode/extensions.json are such files; jq cannot read them. A later format key of a [files] table wins over this default.
decisions.rejected: jq on every .json target (it fails on .vscode/settings.json); a fixed list of JSONC paths in the engine.

decisions.decision: What becomes of the gomplate checks after the engine starts gomplate with mise x gomplate@latest?
decisions.ruling: repo_sync no longer checks command -v gomplate; it checks command -v mise and returns 2 without it. The gate code:lint:repo-sync keeps its mise x -- which gomplate check, so a commit without gomplate stays silent, and the [mise.tools.gomplate] table of tools/repo-sync/tools.toml stays. The #MISE tools.pre-commit line of setup/configs/sync stays.
decisions.rejected: Remove the gate check too (a commit can then need the network); keep the gomplate check of repo_sync (it refuses a run that the wrapper can serve).

decisions.decision: How do the tool wrappers find their files when they run from /?
decisions.ruling: Every path that the engine gives to gomplate, jq or yq is absolute. repo_sync makes the path of the values file absolute at its start; each other path of the engine is already under MISE_PROJECT_ROOT, the clone copy or a temp folder.
decisions.rejected: Run the tools from the current folder (a mise config of the consumer then selects their versions).

decisions.decision: Where does the parse check run on the repo side, and what does a failure do?
decisions.ruling: In the first step of the write of each file (today _rs_file), after the render and after pre-commit autoupdate, before the dprint stage. It runs on every file that the sync writes or compares: a template render, a plain copy, a new seed and a generated mise file. A failure prints '<path>: the result does not parse as <format> - the current file stays', keeps the target as it is, and gives code 2; the other files go on. A dry run reports the same code.
decisions.rejected: A check after dprint (dprint can change a broken file); a check on templates only.

decisions.decision: Which places use the shared header detection?
decisions.ruling: Every place that reads the bootstrap header today: the unblock of a folder path, the removal of a file whose requires file is not there, and the stale removal of the generated mise files. Each reads the first 3 lines and accepts Synced from bootstrap, Synced from repo-config and Generated by macos-setup. The stale removal read only line 1 before; it now reads 3 lines.
decisions.rejected: Keep a separate regex at each place.

decisions.decision: Which part of the selection moves to sync-engine/select?
decisions.ruling: The pack expansion (_rs_pack, _rs_selected) with the packs file, the tool folder, the base pack, the selection and the shown name of the packs file as parameters (the shown name is the fifth argument of _se_selected), and the depth-first depends walk of _rs_resolve. sync-engine/select owns the walk state: _SE_WALK_VISITED (the finished tools in visit order) and the deps of each tool. _se_walk takes two callbacks: the deps callback receives a tool name and prints its dependency names, or returns 2 or 3 after its message; the done callback runs the field checks of a tool when the walk finishes that tool, so the codes and messages come in the order of today. After the walk, repo-sync reads _SE_WALK_VISITED in visit order. The repo-only rules (environments, root_only, seeds, mise owners, extensions) stay in sync-engine/repo-sync.
decisions.rejected: Move all of _rs_resolve (it holds repo-only rules); leave the walk in repo-sync (the Mac front-end then copies it).

decisions.decision: Do the old _rs_ names of the moved functions stay as aliases?
decisions.ruling: No. Each call site in sync-engine/repo-sync calls the _se_ function. The repo-only functions keep their _rs_ names.

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a docs/sync/migrate.md item?
decisions.ruling: No. The parse check reads only the render of the files of bootstrap, and a consumer changes nothing. The docs unit still describes the new code 2.

decisions.decision: Do the tool wrappers need the network when the tool is installed?
decisions.ruling: No. U1 checks with Context7 how mise x <tool>@latest resolves latest. If it can fetch, each wrapper runs MISE_OFFLINE=1 mise x <tool>@latest -- when mise ls --installed <tool> lists a version, else mise x <tool>@latest --. The gate and the tests stay without network.
decisions.rejected: Always mise x <tool>@latest -- (a commit or a test can then need the network).

decisions.decision: What are the details of the parse check?
decisions.ruling: On success, the check discards the stdout and the stderr of jq and yq, so the sync output stays byte equal. yq runs with -p <format> -o json, as B:1229 does. An empty render of a .json target fails with code 2, as B does.
decisions.rejected: Print the tool output on success; accept an empty JSON file.

decisions.decision: Does _rs_file use the shared temp and seed helpers?
decisions.ruling: Yes. _rs_file uses _se_tmp and _se_seed_kept. The temp prefix .sync-engine.XXXXXX replaces .repo-sync.XXXXXX.

decisions.decision: How does _se_record_commit act on a symlink or a file that is not there?
decisions.ruling: _se_record_commit takes an optional new-file header as its last argument. It writes through a symlink to the real file. When the file is not there and a header is given, it creates the file with the header and the key; with no header, a file that is not there is an error (the repo case).
decisions.rejected: A repo-only record function; replace a symlink with a plain file.

decisions.decision: How does a test case run a real write?
decisions.ruling: With case_args=' ' (test line 550 already runs a real write this way). No new CASE_REAL variable.

decisions.decision: Which mode does a new library of sync-engine/ get?
decisions.ruling: Mode 755, as every file of sync-engine/ that has a shebang (plan 1, D18): the check-shebang-scripts-are-executable hook refuses a file with a shebang and no execute bit.
